title: The Dirty Secret of Forward Deployed Engineering — Natalie Meurer, Sierra
talk_summary: A historical/career talk tracing Palantir's forward-deployed engineering from 2008 DevOps through data integration, Slate dashboards, Foundry, and customer enablement, arguing the role has no coherent definition but is converging with product/agent engineering under outcome-based pricing.

takeaways.technique: Customer-accountability as the continuity point across roles
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues every FDE variant (DevOps, data integration, solutioning, enablement) shares one property: direct accountability to a customer outcome, and that this framing should drive what work gets prioritized.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every single forward deployed engineer accountable to the customer, whether that be for devops, for enablement, whether that be for custom solutioning, data integration

takeaways.what_they_do: Observes that as code generation gets cheap, previously separate roles (product eng, infra, DevOps, customer-facing) blur and individuals take on end-to-end ownership.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the lines are blurring. So product engineering is also becoming more client-facing
